message.content:
Below is a concise summary of the key rights and protections you have as a residential tenant in Texas. (This is not legal advice; if you need help with a specific situation, consult an attorney or your local tenant‑rights organization.) | Area | What the law says | Practical tips | |------|-------------------|----------------| | **Security Deposit** | Landlords may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit and two months’ rent for an unfurnished unit. The deposit must be returned within 30 days after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | Keep a written record of the condition of the unit when you move in (photos, video, a signed move‑in checklist). Ask for a receipt of the deposit. | | **Notice Requirements** | • 30‑day notice for month‑to‑month rentals.
• 60‑day notice if the landlord wants to raise the rent or change the lease terms.
• 90‑day notice for terminating a lease longer than one year. | Always give notice in writing and keep a copy. If you’re moving out early, check whether the lease allows early termination or if you can negotiate a “lease break” fee. | | **Habitability** | Landlords must maintain the premises in a safe, sanitary, and livable condition—plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity, pest control, etc. | Report problems promptly in writing. If the landlord fails to fix serious issues, you may be able to withhold rent, repair & deduct, or terminate the lease. | | **Rent Payment** | Rent is due on the date specified in the lease. Late fees are allowed but cannot exceed 5% of the monthly rent. | Pay on time or arrange a payment plan. Keep receipts or bank records. | | **Entry Rights** | Landlords must give at least 24 hours’ written notice before entering, except in emergencies. | Verify that the notice is in writing and that the entry was for a legitimate reason. | | **Discrimination** | Under federal Fair Housing laws and Texas statutes, landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or other protected classes. | Keep records of any discriminatory remarks or actions. File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development if you suspect discrimination. | | **Eviction Process** | A landlord must serve a written notice (usually 3 days for nonpayment, 30 days for lease violations, 90 days for no‑cause termination). After the notice period, the landlord files an unlawful detainer action in court. You have the right to contest the eviction in court. | Respond to notices promptly. If you receive an eviction notice, contact an attorney or a tenant‑rights group immediately. | | **Lease Terms** | The lease is a binding contract. Landlords cannot unilaterally change the lease terms without your consent. | Read the lease carefully before signing. Ask questions about any clause you don’t understand. | | **Right to Repair & Deduct** | If the landlord fails to fix a major problem, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from your rent, provided you follow the proper procedure (written notice, reasonable cost, etc.). | Document all communications and keep receipts. Be prepared to present evidence if the landlord disputes the deduction. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | You have the right to live in the unit without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | Report any harassment or disturbances. If the landlord interferes, you may have grounds to sue for damages. | ### Resources | Resource | What it offers | How to access | |----------|----------------|---------------| | **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division** | Information on landlord‑tenant laws, consumer complaints, and legal assistance. | https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/consumer-protection | | **Texas Commission on Human Rights** | Handles discrimination complaints. | https://www.tchra.org/ | | **Local Tenant‑Rights Organizations** | Free or low‑cost legal clinics, mediation services, and advocacy. | Search online for “tenant rights groups in [your city]” | | **Legal Aid Societies** | Pro bono legal representation for qualifying tenants. | https://www.lawhelp.org/ | | **U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)** | National fair housing resources and complaint filing. | https://www.hud.gov/ | --- #### Quick Checklist Before Signing a Lease 1. **Read the entire lease** – Look for clauses on rent increases, maintenance responsibilities, pet policies, subletting, and termination conditions. 2. **Ask for a copy of the property’s inspection report** – This can help you document the unit’s condition. 3. **Confirm the security deposit amount** – It must not exceed the statutory limit. 4. **Get everything in writing** – Oral agreements are hard to enforce. 5. **Know your local ordinances** – Some cities have additional tenant protections beyond state law. If you have a specific issue (e.g., a dispute over a security deposit, a notice you received, or a maintenance problem), let me know and I can help you draft a formal letter or outline next steps.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are my rights as a tenant in the state of Texas?" They want information about tenant rights. We can provide general info. But we might also offer to generate a contract. The user didn't ask for a contract. So we just answer. No tool needed. Provide overview: security deposit limits, notice requirements, habitability, eviction process, etc. Also mention resources.
